% Invented fixture: overlays under no declared share, which hide. Item specs, an
% inline \uncover, and \pause — the PDF handout gets one page per step with
% pending content hidden in place; HTML keeps one slide with step data.
% \visible keeps its argument's place and ships none of it off its steps. Links
% in pending steps, a set and an item covered again ship only where they show.
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{slides}

\begin{document}

\begin{frame}{Reveal in order}
\begin{itemize}
\item<1-> Always here.
\item<2-> Second beat.
\item<3-> Third beat.
\end{itemize}
\uncover<3>{A closing line for the last step.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Paused}
Before the pause.

\pause
After the pause.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Kept in place}
Before the reveal \visible<2>{a phrase kept in place} and after it.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Linked steps}
Read \href{https://example.org/first}{the first page}.
\begin{itemize}
\item<-2> Early \href{https://example.org/early}{note}.
\item<1,3> Every other \href{https://example.org/other}{beat}.
\end{itemize}
\uncover<2->{Later \href{https://example.org/later}{reading}.}
\end{frame}

\end{document}
